issues.detail: Only the local pass and a bare LLM call are runnable code; the judge prompt/RULESET is never defined, the score-averaging and combination logic is not shown, and the GPTZero/Originality.ai step is delegated to external docs.
The LLM-judge layer is hard-wired to the Anthropic SDK and ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, and the skill gives no guidance for using a different model provider.

The examples are short text excerpts showing pseudo-output only; the 'Local score' and 'Combined score' values are not produced by the provided code, and Example 1 lists 'research shows' as a found phrase although it is not in the PHRASES list, so the examples are inconsistent with the code and cannot be reproduced.

scenarios.name: local-burstiness-and-phrase-pass
scenarios.rationale: A computes burstiness as sd/mean, checks case-insensitive phrases, and states that above 0.5 leans human and below 0.3 leans AI as rough heuristics to calibrate on known texts; B computes CV but uses different cut-offs (0.55/0.40), never gives 0.5/0.3, and only says it hasn't validated them, without advising calibration on known-origin texts.

scenarios.name: llm-judge-call-with-safe-handling
scenarios.rationale: B matches the rubric closely: it uses the requested fields (score 0-10, verdict, confidence, signals_found, reasoning, suspicious_phrases), reads the model from an env var, retries once on validation failure, and tells the judge the article is untrusted data. A also reads the model from an env var and treats the article as data, but it omits the requested fields (it has ai_likelihood 0-1, signals and rationale, with no verdict, suspicious_phrases or signals_found), and it has no retry on parse failure. A also has a hardcoded default model name, though it can be overridden by the env var.

scenarios.name: student-essay-fairness-review
scenarios.rationale: B explicitly covers all three rubric points (the under-200-word rule so no automated score, the Stanford TOEFL false-positive finding with raising thresholds or not auto-flagging, and score-is-not-proof with routing to a human reviewer), while A covers the non-native bias and not-sole-evidence points well but gives only a vague short-text threshold (250–300 words) and never states the under-200 skip rule or human-reviewer routing.
